arxiv-1710-01712.title: Note on “The Complexity of Counting Surjective Homomorphisms and Compactions”
arxiv-1710-01712.creator: Holger Dell
arxiv-1710-01712.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by Holger Dell. Focke, Goldberg, and Živný [ 4 ] prove a complexity dichotomy for the problem of counting surjective homomorphisms from a large input graph G G without loops to a fixed graph H H that may have loops. In this note, we give a short proof of a weaker result: Namely, we only prove the # ​ P \#\mathrm{P} -hardness of the more general problem in which G G may have loops.

arxiv-2111-02849.title: Microscopic theory of ionic motion in solids
arxiv-2111-02849.creator: Aleksandr Rodin, Keian Noori, Alexandra Carvalho, and A. H. Castro Neto
arxiv-2111-02849.description: Abstract Drag and diffusion of mobile ions in solids are of interest for both purely theoretical and applied scientific communities. This article proposes a theoretical description of ion drag in solids that can be used to estimate ionic conductivities in crystals, and forms a basis for the rational design of solid electrolyte materials.

arxiv-2201-00209.title: Cobordism invariants for knots with two indices
arxiv-2201-00209.creator: V.O.Manturov
arxiv-2201-00209.description: Abstract We construct an invariant of virtual knots which is a sliceness obstruction and sensitive to the Δ \Delta -move. This invariants works if ℤ 2 ⊕ ℤ 2 \mathbb{Z}_{2}\oplus\mathbb{Z}_{2} -index of chords is present. Keywords: knot, invariant, virtual knot, parity, sliceness, group.

arxiv-2208-08792.creator: Prashant Singh, Saikat Santra, Anupam Kundu
arxiv-2208-08792.description: Abstract We study the extreme value statistics of a run and tumble particle (RTP) in one dimension till its first passage to the origin starting from the position x 0 ( > 0 ) x_{0}~(>0) . This model has recently drawn a lot of interest due to its biological application in modelling the motion of certain species of bacteria.

arxiv-2209-14107.title: Debiasing Graph Neural Networks via Learning Disentangled Causal Substructure
arxiv-2209-14107.creator: Shaohua Fan, Xiao Wang, Yanhu Mo, Chuan Shi, Jian Tang
arxiv-2209-14107.description: Abstract Most Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) predict the labels of unseen graphs by learning the correlation between the input graphs and labels. However, by presenting a graph classification investigation on the training graphs with severe bias, surprisingly, we discover that GNNs always tend to explore the spurious correlations to make decision, even if the causal correlation always exists.

arxiv-2305-14241.title: Paradox with Phase-Coupled Interferometers

arxiv-2305-14241.description: Abstract A pair of interferometers can be coupled by allowing one path from each to overlap such that if the particles meet in this overlap region, they annihilate. It was shown by one of us over thirty years ago that such annihilation-coupled interferometers can exhibit apparently paradoxical behaviour. More recently, Bose et al .

arxiv-2307-00879.title: Geometric renormalization of weighted networks
arxiv-2307-00879.creator: Muhua Zheng, Guillermo García-Pérez, Marián Boguñá, M. Ángeles Serrano
arxiv-2307-00879.description: Abstract The geometric renormalization technique for complex networks has successfully revealed the multiscale self-similarity of real network topologies and can be applied to generate replicas at different length scales. In this letter, we extend the geometric renormalization framework to weighted networks, where the intensities of the interactions play a crucial role in their structural organization and function.

arxiv-2307-13545.description: Abstract Direct detection of the Cosmic Dawn and Epoch of Reionization via the redshifted 21-cm line of neutral Hydrogen will have unprecedented implications for studying structure formation in the early Universe. This exciting goal is challenged by the difficulty of extracting the faint 21-cm signal buried beneath bright astrophysical foregrounds and contaminated by numerous systematics.

arxiv-2510-23931.creator: Miguel Fernandez-de-Retana, Unai Zulaika, Rubén Sánchez-Corcuera, Aitor Almeida
arxiv-2510-23931.description: Abstract Federated Learning (FL) allows for the training of Machine Learning models in a collaborative manner without the need to share sensitive data. However, it remains vulnerable to Gradient Leakage Attacks (GLAs), which can reveal private information from the shared model updates.

pmc-12555890.title: Lemierre-like syndrome and severe descending mediastinitis in an Infant with retropharyngeal abscess due to methicillin susceptible Staphylococcus aureus
pmc-12555890.creator: Shreya Chandran, Wimwipa Mongkonsritragoon, Ji-Yeon Kim, Nirupama Kannikeswaran, Nahed Abdel-Haq
pmc-12555890.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). An 11-month-old girl presented with fever, respiratory distress and septic shock. She had no neck stiffness, swelling, difficulty swallowing, or drooling. An echocardiogram that was done to evaluate cardiac function showed compression of the innominate vein. Subsequent cross-sectional imaging revealed retropharyngeal abscess (RPA) with extensive descending mediastinitis and abscesses as well as septic thrombophlebitis involving the left internal jugular vein, subclavian vein, and innominate vein, consistent with Lemierre-like syndrome. Blood cultures grew methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA).

pmc-12575526.title: Do eye trackers estimate eyeball rotation? The relationship between tracked eye image feature and estimated saccadic waveform
pmc-12575526.creator: Marcus Nyström, Diederick C. Niehorster, Roy S. Hessels, Richard Andersson, Marta K. Skrok, Robert Konklewski, Patrycjusz Stremplewski, Maciej Nowakowski, Jakub Lipiński, Szymon Tamborski, Anna Szkulmowska, Maciej Szkulmowski, Ignace T. C. Hooge
pmc-12575526.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The eyeball is not rigid and deforms during saccades. As a consequence, the saccade waveform recorded by an eye tracker may depend on which structure of the eye is used to estimate eyeball rotation. Here, we systematically describe and compare signals co-recorded from the retina, the cornea (corneal reflection, CR), the pupil, and the lens (fourth Purkinje reflection, P4) during saccades. We found that several commonly used parameters for saccade characterization differ systematically across the signals.
